title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from p.138: S is a base on which 2 is invertible. H is a smooth group scheme over S of relative dimension 1, for example G_m, G_a or an elliptic curve. X is an H-torsor, and \omega_0 is the invariant cotangent line. On p.138 Grothendieck showed two things. First, translation-invariant affine connections (1-jets) correspond to sections of a torsor under \omega_0^2 inside V_0\otimes\omega_0. Second, the projective bundle P carries a canonical section \sigma, and there is a canonical choice, the 'Campbell-Hausdorff' one, coming from the group law. Here V_0 is the rank-3 bundle of the projective (PGL_2) structure, with V_0 \supset L_0 \supset \omega_0.

This page adds the following.

(1) A translation-invariant extension 0\to O_X\to F\to O_X\to 0 gives an H-equivariant isomorphism P \simeq \mathbb{P}(F). The complement of the canonical section is then identified with the O_X-torsor attached to the extension class. Grothendieck calls the induced structure on O_X 'hyperbolic'. For an elliptic curve with nonzero class this is Atiyah's indecomposable bundle F_2. It is the familiar fact that the rank-2 oper bundle J^1(\omega^{-1/2}) on an elliptic curve is the nontrivial self-extension of O.

(2) The section of P fixed by this identification is disjoint from the canonical section 0. It therefore gives a splitting V \simeq \omega\oplus O_X\oplus\omega^{-1} in which O_X+\omega^{-1} and \omega^{-1} are stable under the connection. The connection then induces the 'hyperbolic' connection on the O_X piece. Grothendieck compares this splitting with the Campbell-Hausdorff splitting of p.138.

(3) Classification of invariant projective connections. After an invariant trivialisation of \omega, these are the operators \partial^2+c, with c an invariant section. The flat P^1-bundle has invariant horizontal sections given by the eigenlines of the constant matrix [[0,c],[1,0]].
- For c\neq0 there are two such lines, since 2 is invertible. The structure group then reduces invariantly to a torus-type subgroup of PGL(\mathbb{P}(\omega_0+O)).
- For c=0 the matrix is nilpotent, with a single line, giving unipotent reduction.

So over an algebraically closed field, the canonical projective connection is characterised among invariant ones by this property: P has exactly one invariant horizontal section. Every other invariant projective connection has exactly two.

(4) NB: suppose H is proper with connected fibres, so X/S is a torsor under an elliptic curve. Projective connections form a torsor under \Gamma(\omega^2), and \omega^2 is trivial with constant global sections. Hence every projective connection is H-invariant. The criterion in (3) then characterises the canonical projective connection (the uniformisation by the additive group) among all projective connections on X.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the argument is a sketch with lacunae, and parts are illegible.

The 'exactly two invariant horizontal sections' claim needs 2 invertible and an algebraically closed (or suitably split) base. Without splitting, the two eigenlines may only be defined over a quadratic extension. Grothendieck partly flags this with the '?' in the margin.

ideas.what: Identify the projective bundle of the invariant projective structure on a 1-dimensional group torsor with \mathbb{P}(F), F a translation-invariant self-extension of O_X
ideas.modern_name: Oper bundle on an elliptic curve = Atiyah's indecomposable bundle F_2 (rank-2 oper / indigenous bundle)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Atiyah (1957) for F_2; Gunning for indigenous bundles; Beilinson–Drinfeld for opers

ideas.what: Classify invariant projective connections \partial^2+c by the number of invariant horizontal sections: unipotent for c=0, two eigenlines with torus reduction otherwise
ideas.modern_name: Projective structures on tori / monodromy of PGL_2-opers on elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning; Loray–Marín (projective structures on elliptic curves)

ideas.what: On an elliptic-curve torsor every projective connection is invariant, so the canonical (group-law) one is intrinsically characterised
ideas.modern_name: Canonical projective structure (uniformisation by G_a) on an elliptic curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Gunning); arithmetic version: Mochizuki's indigenous bundles

missed.claim: This is a relative, characteristic-free (only 2 invertible) treatment of invariant projective connections on torsors under any smooth 1-dimensional group scheme over S. The canonical 'Campbell-Hausdorff' projective connection is characterised by unipotent reduction of the structure group. This is a uniform scheme-theoretic version of classical facts, written down long before Mochizuki's p-adic indigenous bundles. The content is standard; only the generality and the date are of historical interest.
missed.quote: la connexion proj. can. est caractérisée, parmi celles qui sont invariantes, par la condition que P n'admette que une seule droite stable invariante
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only a minor historical datum on Grothendieck's early-1970s interest in projective connections and opers within his Gauss-Manin / Cartier programme. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct but routine computation of invariant projective connections on elliptic curves and other 1-dimensional groups. The facts are classical, though the relative framework over S is mildly notable as a historical datum.
transcription_corrections: The first line probably reads 'Si extension'/'Soit extension' (or an abbreviation) rather than 'Ext extension'.
'G-iso' is likely 'H-iso' (equivariant for the group H).
The subgroup is probably of GL/PGL(\mathbb{P}(\omega_0+O)), consistent with p.138's \mathbb{P}(\omega_0+\omega_0^{-1}).
In the NB, the illegible phrase is likely 'sont invariantes par H', i.e. all projective connections on X are invariant under H.
